question: If tan x = cot(3x - 30°), find x.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If tan A = cot B, then A + B = 90°.

Substituting A = x and B = 3x − 30°:

⇒ x + (3x − 30°) = 90°

⇒ 4x = 120° ⇒ x = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan x = cot(3x − 30°)

**Concept Used:**

cot θ = tan(90° − θ)

**Calculation:**

⇒ tan x = tan(90° − (3x − 30°))

Comparing the angles on both sides:

⇒ x = 90° − (3x − 30°)

⇒ x = 90° − 3x + 30°

⇒ x + 3x = 120°

⇒ 4x = 120°

⇒ x = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles Rule

When the sum of two angles is 90°, they are known as complementary angles. The values of their respective trigonometric co-functions are always equal.

Trigonometric Co-function Identities

sin θ = cos(90° − θ) | sec θ = cosec(90° − θ) | tan θ = cot(90° − θ)

Important Values at 30°

tan 30° = 1/√3 and cot 30° = √3
